gaps.sentence: The debt ___ (repay) in full by May, he promised.
gaps.explanation: Reported future passive: would be + past participle after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: We had the whole house ___ (repaint) before the wedding.
gaps.explanation: 'Had the house repainted' — painters did it at our request. Object + past participle.

gaps.sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
gaps.explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.

gaps.sentence: My usual barber's chair ___ (fix), so I'm trying a new salon.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + fixed for an unfinished, ongoing repair.

gaps.sentence: The passengers ___ to fasten their seatbelts as the plane entered the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'The passengers were told to …' — passive of 'tell somebody to do'.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript ___ (BELIEVE) to be the composer’s last work.
gaps.explanation: 'People believe it is…' becomes 'it is believed to be…'.

gaps.sentence: This wall ___ (build) centuries ago — no modern tool leaves marks like these.
gaps.explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + built to draw a conclusion about the past.

gaps.sentence: These wetlands ___ (threaten) by pollution every single year.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive with the agent introduced by 'by': are threatened by.
